**Isosyll v4.2.1 on one CPU core: final 4.24% panel WER · 2.34% full-DEV dev-clean · 14.8× real time · live 28.5× real time at 0.366 J/audio-s**

![Isosyll: Always Listening, Barely Computing. Single-core throughput vs. pooled WER for all 12 timed public CPU speech recognizers and Isosyll final and live on the 730-utterance LibriSpeech DEV panel, names colored by energy per audio-second](docs/paper/money.png)

**Figure 1.** Isosyll v4.2.1 vs. all 12 timed public CPU speech recognizers on one pinned Zen 2 core: the utterance-end final pass reaches 4.24% WER (2.63% dev-clean) at 14.8× and 0.721 J/audio-s, vs. Zipformer INT8 at 5.25% (3.03% dev-clean), 14.0× and 0.573 J/audio-s; live +LM (v4.2.1: content-word rerank at endpoints) runs at 28.5× (0.366 J/audio-s, 4.58% WER at 160 ms; −0.46 pp vs. Zipformer on unselected DEV); J/audio-s from the paired full-panel runs (R9 for v4.2.0 final, R10 for v4.2.1 live, R6 for Zipformer). [Paper](docs/paper/paper.pdf) · [Release record](docs/ultra/releases/v4.2.1.md).

- **Lowest Isosyll WER yet (final, unchanged since v4.2.0).** The utterance-end final pass (the `isosyll transcribe` default) reaches **4.24%** panel WER (**2.63%** dev-clean) and **4.32%** full DEV (**2.34%** dev-clean) at **14.8×** real time and **0.721 J/audio-s**. On the unselected DEV C-half it is −0.93 [−1.23, −0.66] pp, lower WER vs. Zipformer INT8 and −0.66 [−0.79, −0.55] pp, lower WER vs. v4.1.0 final; it costs **+10.3%** CPU vs. v4.1.0 final (its beam-48 confidence gate **+5.0%**, at its 5% budget, locked by owner choice; paired R9 full-panel blocks).
- **Fastest, with the lowest measured energy.** On one quiet Zen 2 core, **Isosyll live** (160 ms chunks, +LM) runs at **28.5×** real time and **0.366 J/audio-s** (**4.58%** panel, **2.74%** dev-clean, **4.79%** full DEV WER, **659 MB** RAM): **2.0×** the paired throughput of Zipformer INT8 at **63%** of its energy per audio-second (paired R10 full-panel blocks).
- **New in v4.2.1: live endpoint rerank.** At each live endpoint whose top-2 beam margin is below 3.75 (about 59% of endpoints), a content-word t2 rerank picks the committed text: full DEV live WER **4.79%** (v4.1.0/v4.2.0 live 5.32%; unselected C-half −0.55 [−0.66, −0.45] pp, lower WER). It costs **+7.5%** CPU, **+9.4%** energy and **+329 MB** RAM vs. v4.2.0 live, and adds **11.0 ms** median / **65.8 ms** p95 of single-core compute at each utterance end (paired R10 blocks).
- **Two small artifacts.** A 60 MB INT8 model per mode (live: v4.1.0 weights, unchanged; final: a new weight average), same architecture and engine; live mode now also loads the final pass's M5 LM and t2 rescorer for its endpoint rerank; streaming keeps the v4.1.0 commit pass.
- **Bit-exact pure-Rust engine.** No external runtime or BLAS (AVX2, AVX-512 VNNI, ARM NEON, scalar), with identical transcripts across **18** cross-ISA witness runs.

Measured on one pinned Zen 2 core (730-utterance LibriSpeech DEV selection panel; § = 73-clip timing subset, ‡ = shared-host H0 interim). Unselected DEV C-half, v4.2.1 live vs. Zipformer INT8: −0.46 [−0.66, −0.28] pp, lower WER. J/audio-s: idle-subtracted core J per audio-second (CPU-domain registers only, not wall power): comparators from the R7 matched campaign (73-clip subset, median of 2–3 core-clean blocks), Isosyll final from the R9 and live from the R10 full-panel blocks under the same protocol. The 0.366 J/audio-s and 63% above are the paired R10 full-panel run. Exploratory DEV-only results. Both modes meet their registered edit gates: final (v4.2.0) and, since the v4.2.1 endpoint rerank, live (662 panel edits vs. the 722 gate; v4.1.0/v4.2.0 live, 734, was released by owner decision after missing it). The owner chose the rerank's timed setting (margin 3.75); both modes were selected on the DEV selection half and checked once on the unselected half (protocol and limits in the [paper](docs/paper/paper.pdf) and [release record](docs/ultra/releases/v4.2.1.md)).
